column1: EDIT_DISTANCE, EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY, and JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE were introduced in SQL Server {{c1::2025}}.
column2:
The boxed SQL Server version matters because older releases lack these built-ins. Azure availability can follow different release rules.
Review source

column1: To enable the SQL Server 2025 fuzzy-function preview, run ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET {{c1::PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON}};
column2:
Enable the setting in the database that runs the comparison. It is not a server-wide setting.
Review source

column1: EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY returns an integer from {{c1::0 to 100}}.
column2:
This is a normalized similarity score, not a count. Compare using a lower bound when requiring a minimum similarity.
Review source

No edits are needed, so this identical pair earns the maximum score. A missing input is not the same as an exact match.
Review source

The function cannot score an absent value. Handle SQL NULL separately rather than interpreting it as a dissimilar pair.
Review source

column1: To require edit similarity of at least 80, use WHERE EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY(@a, @b) {{c1::>=}} 80.
column2:
The lower bound admits scores of 80 and above. Do not reverse the comparison as you would for a maximum distance.
Review source

column1: For closest-first results, sort a score from EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY using ORDER BY Score {{c1::DESC}}.
column2:
The descending sort puts a score of 95 before a score of 80. Add a unique key if ties need a predictable order.
Review source

column1: JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE uses a scale from {{c1::0 to 1}}.
column2:
An exact match is at zero. Larger values indicate a greater distance by this measure.
Review source

Identical text has no Jaro-Winkler distance. A similarity score instead puts an exact match at the high end of its scale.
Review source

column1: To allow Jaro-Winkler distance at most 0.05, use WHERE JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE(@a, @b) {{c1::<=}} 0.05.
column2:
The upper bound includes 0.05 itself. Tune the cutoff with examples of true and false matches.
Review source

column1: For closest-first results, sort a score from JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE using ORDER BY Distance {{c1::ASC}}.
column2:
Ascending puts 0.02 before 0.10. That is the opposite of a higher-is-better similarity sort.
Review source

The return type can express fractional distance. Do not interpret the result as a count of changed characters.
Review source

The result is enough to show that this pair fails the threshold. It does not assert an exact uncapped distance.

column1: A supported Windows collation can be applied to a fuzzy function's arguments using the {{c1::COLLATE}} clause.
column2:
Apply the collation to the input expressions that need it. This keeps the change local to the comparison.
Review source

column1: To accept strings needing at most three edits, use WHERE EDIT_DISTANCE(@a, @b) {{c1::<=}} 3.
column2:
The predicate includes a distance of exactly three. Smaller distances represent closer matches.
